definition: Ambiguous or open to more than one interpretation.
example: The test produced equivocal evidence, so the investigators collected another sample.
nuance: Equivocal describes ambiguity; ambivalent describes mixed feelings.
prompt: The statement leaves it unclear whether the committee supports the proposal.
options: The committee offered an equivocal response that could be read as approval or refusal.
The committee gave an equivocal refusal, making its opposition unmistakable.
Both candidates earned an equivocal number of votes: exactly 200 each.
reasons: This sentence demonstrates the meaning: ambiguous or open to more than one interpretation.
An unmistakable refusal is unambiguous, the opposite of equivocal.
Equal quantities are equivalent or equal, not equivocal.
